messages:
meera: FYI customer (skylytics) on Private VPC reporting intermittent TLS handshake failures calling our inference endpoint /v1/generate. They get 502/TLS errors from their app. Root logs show cert mismatch and IP hits. Repro steps attached — high severity, customer impact.

ben: Can you paste the minimal repro (dig/openssl/curl) and traceroute? also which VPC DNS resolver are they using?

meera: Pasting what I ran from their jumpbox (10.0.5.12) — note the UDP dig truncates, TCP succeeds: 
```
$ dig @10.0.5.53 example-model.redwood.ai +short
;; Truncated, retrying in TCP...

$ dig @10.0.5.53 example-model.redwood.ai +tcp +short
models-edge.hosting.redwood.ai.
198.51.100.23
```
They reported their app-level resolver only used UDP and then fell back to a cached A record that resolves to 198.51.100.23 (edge IP). When connecting they see TLS cert CN mismatch.

jordan: can you paste the openssl output?

meera: sure: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 198.51.100.23:443 
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood, CN = Redwood Root CA
...
subject=/CN=*.hosting.redwood.ai
issuer=/CN=Redwood Root CA
---
140735...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
*** Certificate is for *.hosting.redwood.ai -- client expected example-model.redwood.ai ***
```
This matches customer ticket where their app reports cert name mismatch.

alex: hypothesis: their VPC egress NACL/SG allows UDP/53 but blocks TCP/53. EDNS0 causes responses >512 bytes and UDP gets truncated; proper resolution requires TCP/53 to fetch the full CNAME chain (models-edge.hosting...). Their resolver/client falls back to stale A or an incomplete answer and ends up connecting in a way that triggers the wrong cert. TL;DR: DNS over TCP being blocked -> bad/partial resolve -> TLS problems.

alex: action items / recommended firewall changes: 
- Allow outbound TCP port 53 to their configured resolver(s) (10.0.5.53 or their forwarders).
- Ensure outbound ephemeral port range (1024-65535) is allowed for return traffic on the NACL/SG (many NACLs accidentally deny ephemeral return ports).
- Add allow rule for outbound to our edge IP ranges on 443 if they want a narrowed allowlist.
Examples: 
```
# NACL (stateless) - outbound allow (higher priority than broad deny)
- Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 53 from 10.0.0.0/16 to 10.0.5.53/32
- Rule 110: ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 from 10.0.0.0/16 to 0.0.0.0/0
# Security Group (stateful) - egress
- Allow: TCP 53 to 10.0.5.53/32
- Allow: TCP 443 to 198.51.100.0/24  (our edge IP block)
```

ben: also check if their DNS resolver does DNSSEC/EDNS0 with large responses. If UDP 512 cap hits, people must permit TCP fallback. Another quick check for them: `dig +short @10.0.5.53 +bufsize=4096 example-model.redwood.ai` and `dig +tcp` — if +tcp differs from plain UDP, that's the sign.

jordan: added repro with curl +resolve to confirm behavior: 
```
# simulating bad path (direct IP)
curl -v --resolve example-model.redwood.ai:443:198.51.100.23 https://example-model.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# good path (ensures correct name resolution via cname)
# curl with proper host resolution should succeed; if client library skips SNI or uses IP it can fail.
```

alex: TL;DR and suggested customer message: "Please update your NACL/Security Group to allow outbound TCP/53 to your DNS forwarders and ensure ephemeral return ports are permitted. Alternatively, add our edge IP ranges to a 443 egress allowlist to avoid relying on resolving large CNAME chains. After change, verify with `dig +tcp` and retry your app." :thumbsup:

ticket-bot: Created INC-2026-4578 for skylytics — assigned to support-team, priority P1. https://rwd/tickets/INC-2026-4578

customer-ops: Thank you — we'll push the NACL changes (allow TCP/53 and open return ports) and report back in ~30m. Appreciated! :pray:

meera: Thanks — I'll keep the ticket warm and coordinate with eng if the edge IP whitelist approach is requested.

ben: If they still see issues after changes, capture tcpdump of 53 traffic (pcap) + `dig @10.0.5.53 +tcp` output and paste here.

customer-ops: Will do.
